name: Script (1981)
description: Muse Air's only scheme, worn from its first flight in July 1981 until it became TranStar in February 1986: an all-white aircraft with 'Muse Air' brushed big along the forward fuselage in a deep purple script, its r's tail running on as a long level stroke under the windows (aft on the left side, forward to the nose on the right), and the same script smaller on the fin, rising toward the tail. A black anti-glare panel runs from the flight deck windows to the nose's top. Grey wings, white nacelles with polished lips.
notes: Drawn on the MD-80, from N930MC (left side 1985, right side 1984) and an undated Douglas photo. Muse Air's DC-9-51s (from 1983) are drawn on it too until their own shape is in; no openly licensed photo of one in this paint was found, so they're assumed to match. The two sides were lettered differently: the right side's script is about 8% shorter and sits farther forward, so each side has its own title. The purple is read off color film and could be a little bluer or redder.

sources.title: Muse Air MD-82; N930MC@MSY, February 1984 (CC BY-SA 2.0, Aero Icarus)
sources.note: MD-82 N930MC, right side, side-on, New Orleans, February 1984 (flipped nose-left and fitted to shapes/MD82.json with tools/photo_trace.py from the windows, exits and crown, within about 0.3 m aft of the cockpit): the script's heights and its run on the right side, the fin script's run and slope, the anti-glare panel, the white nacelles and grey wings. The sharpest of the three; the wordmark's proportions follow it.

sources.title: 5-10-85 Los Angeles N930MC (CC BY 2.0, Pete Macklin)
sources.note: MD-82 N930MC, left side, Los Angeles, 5 October 1985 (fitted to shapes/MD82.json by both passenger doors, both exits, the nose and the crown, within 7 px): the left side's script from just behind the forward door to the swash's end over the second exit, the anti-glare panel's lower edge, the fin script reading up toward the tail. Taken from a little above and soft, so its heights are only a check.

sources.title: Catalog-26_0007603 413876515 Piction ID Muse Air Plane (public domain, San Diego Air & Space Museum Archives)
sources.note: An MD-80 in Muse Air's paint, left side from ahead, undated (about 1981): the script's heights against the windows and swash (the same as the right side's), its run from the forward door to the exits, the anti-glare panel to the nose's top, the fin script rising toward the tail.

sources.title: Muse Air (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Dates: first flights 15 July 1981 (MD-80s), bought by Southwest in 1985, renamed TranStar Airlines in February 1986, shut down 9 August 1987.

sources.title: Untitled McDonnell Douglas DC-9-51 HB-ISR (CC BY 2.0, Kambui)
sources.note: DC-9-51 HB-ISR stripped to bare metal at Zurich in 1983 for its delivery flight to Muse Air: evidence that the DC-9-51s came from Swissair, not of their paint.

areas.name: black anti-glare panel round the flight deck windows, tapering forward to the nose's top

titles.style: Muse Air's script: 'Muse Air' brushed in one heavy, fast hand, the letters leaning hard forward. A blob and a thin flick lead into a tall zigzag M; 'use' is small and joined; the A is a big leaning loop rising above the rest, then i (dotted) and r, whose tail runs on as a long level brush stroke under the windows. Drawn as a mark (no typeface comes close).
